definitions.E5:
Thanks—your program is **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering**.

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Length:** Four years of academic study  
- **Pathway:** Successful completion of the first two years awards a **Civil Engineering Diploma**. Students may continue into the final two years if they meet the continuation requirements.
- **Program focus:** Civil engineering fundamentals, surveying, materials testing, drafting, engineering software, construction and project management, and a team-based CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project.
- **Status:** Active

The program includes core coursework, Level 4 electives, technical electives in Levels 7–8, and optional co-op work terms. The official program information is available at:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/

To check whether you can graduate now, tell me which courses you told me you have completed, or specify that you completed all courses through a particular level.
definitions.E2: Please list the courses you told me you completed, using their course codes and names. Alternatively, tell me whether you completed **all courses through a particular level**. Then I can check your Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering graduation requirements.
definitions.E3:
Thanks for clarifying. I’ll treat this as: **you told me you completed all courses through Level 4** in the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** program.

You **cannot be confirmed as graduated yet** based on that information. The verified program record describes the BEng as four years of full-time academic study, and the curriculum continues through **Levels 5–8**. Remaining required coursework includes, for example:

- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7021 — Mechanics of Materials 2**
- **CIVL 7001 — Engineering and Society**
- **CIVL 7023 — Engineering Dynamics**
- **CIVL 7030 — Civil Engineering Contracts and Law**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**
- **OPMT 7031 — Engineering Economics**

Level 4 also includes a choice of **two Level 4 electives**. **CIVL 5990 — Cooperative Education Work Term 1** is an optional co-op work term, not a substitute for the remaining academic levels.

The first two years may lead to the **Civil Engineering Diploma**; completing Level 4 alone does not establish completion of the BEng. I cannot verify your graduation eligibility or any continuation requirements from the available data, so please confirm with the program office.

Program information: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/
definitions.E7: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
